statements.text: Verbatim Quote Sheet — Metro Council 10/06/26, Resolution RS2026-2264 (Motorola / CAD)
Source: Metro Nashville Network YouTube (wNHXllwtgBk), 4h25m.

Cross-read: (1) YouTube Google auto-captions, (2) mlx-whisper large-v3-turbo full pass, (3) mlx-whisper no-context recovery pass over 01:56:40–04:21:40 (the original pass had a 2h10m decode loop that destroyed the debate; the recovery pass restored it).
Timestamps are video-clock HH:MM:SS.
All quotes below agree across reads except where noted.
The "tautology" (Allen / Rosenberg) Council Member Allen, 02:24:14: "We had a speaker at the beginning of the meeting that asked ...
could we add a sentence that says anything that would be acquired that is subject to Section 13808, which is the surveillance section, would have to comply with that section.
And so I would like to ask legal to respond.
If something is subject to 1308, it would have to comply with that section.
Is there any circumstance where it's a small enough addition to the contract that it would slide under ...
by passing this resolution, if there is an addition made later that is subject to that ...?"
Dave Rosenberg (mayor's office), 02:26:07: "Please correct me if I'm answering the wrong question.
You cannot use this contract for things covered under the surveillance code because to approve something under the surveillance code, it requires a public hearing for approval.
If you're asking whether you could put language that says that you can't -- basically that you can't break the law -- yes."

Rosenberg again, 02:27:30: "Yes, because in order to approve any surveillance use or a contract that includes surveillance uses, it has to be passed by resolution with a public hearing before council there.
I mean, by definition, by not having a public hearing, there is no opportunity to do that."

Ellis / "pen and paper" / "no backup plan" Council Member Ellis, 02:21:19: "It just sort of alarms me that it's being deferred one meeting, but then we hear that they may or may not extend it in good faith.
So I wonder what happens if they decide to not extend it in good faith?
Like, what's the backup plan?"
"I'm just going to address it to the administration table, whether that's the mayor's office or legal.
What would the hypothetical backup plan be?"
"Yes."
[asked: "Would Motorola not extend in good faith for two more weeks?"]
Rosenberg, 02:22:05: "Council member, there isn't a backup plan.
Pen and paper."
Ellis: "Unfortunately, yes."
[asked: "does that fully answer your question?"]

Spain's "pad and paper" (first use) Council Member Spain, 02:04:19: "If this is not renewed, uh, Department of Emergency Communications has said they'll have to go back to, uh, a pad and paper basically to handle dispatch to make sure that NFD and MNPD are getting to where they need to go to take care of our citizens."
The expired contract / website / 2009 Council Member Welsh, 02:09:52: "I once again would like to ask my colleagues to support a two meeting deferral so that we can get a copy of this contract.
We can compare what we have in the new contract to the old contract ..."
Welsh, 02:13:20: "One is why the existing contract is not on a government website, and my understanding is that the existing contract that expired in June did not have CAD in it ..."
Macy Amos (Metro Legal), 02:14:39: "Macy Amos from Metro Legal.
I am certain that the contract is online.
I will find it and send it to you tonight."
Vice Mayor, 02:14:51: "Miss Amos, if you would please send it to special counsel Wilson so he can send it to the entirety of the body, that would be great."
Council Member Sepulveda, 02:16:01: "I'm hearing that their last contract that's on the website is from 2009.
Also, apparently we've been operating without a contract since June or July."
Council Member Benedict, 02:20:26: "I don't feel comfortable right now having not reviewed the existing contract because it's not available.
And the fact that we could get it later tonight is great, but that's not before a vote right now."
Evans-Segal Council Member Evans-Segal, 02:28:01: "I just wanted to rise to explain that I'm going to vote to support this tonight ...

But I also just want to say we wouldn't be here if — three years into this term — we were still not getting things way, way later than we should be on a contract where this apparently they could just stop servicing us tomorrow and we'd be on pen and paper.
And this contract just came to us — how recently ago — and how long was it expired before it came before this body?"
"I think it is embarrassing as a city that we have been operating this way."
"And I also think we wouldn't be here if the community believed that we were good at self-policing the use of surveillance.
We've seen this term with FUSIS, ALPRs, Leocyte, 5CAST, that the administration did not send them through the proper surveillance channels.
Surveillance tech has to go through the proper surveillance tech channels.
That is the law.
I am going to vote for this because I believe the administration wants to follow the law.
But when we get things months after they're expired, we get these arguments that the whole system could crash if we don't vote for it.
And we know we've been misled in the past."
FUSIS / drones on the floor Council Member Pul(v)a, 02:31:41: "I have a question for the administration whether FUSES and CAD have been integrated."
has it already been integrated with FUSES, or does it have the possibility of being integrated with FUSES for its enhancement?
Does it have the functionality?"
Rosenberg, 02:32:13 / 02:32:55: "I don't know how FUSIS[?] and CAD ...
I know that pretty much any software can be integrated with any software.
This is the same CAD that we are currently using, and it has not been integrated with FUSIS.
We do not use FUSIS in Nashville."
The vote Vice Mayor, 02:34:10: "This resolution has passed with 26 votes in favor, seven votes against, and one abstention."
Deferral votes on record: two-meeting deferral failed 10–24 (02:11:18); one-meeting deferral with re-referral failed 14–20 (02:23:08); motion to call the previous question failed 20–14 (02:31:14).

Contract surfaced after the vote (end of meeting) Special counsel, 04:22:28: "Council members, we have identified legislation that we believe is the latest contract that has been approved by this body.
However, at this hour, we are waiting confirmation from ECD to make sure that that is the correct contract.
I have a commitment from the Department of Law that once we have that commitment, I will receive the legislation and we will forward it to you in the morning."
Council Member Johnson, 04:22:59: "I'm just wondering why these contracts aren't on the documents portal.
The last contract with Motorola for ECD expired in 2009 and was ...
destroyed by some order because it's literally 17 years old.
So we've had no public documentation of whatever contract with Motorola for 17 years.
I just want to know why it's not on the portal."

Your own public comment (Michael Lacy, 00:23:17–00:25:33) Recorded and in all reads: "This resolution and the associated contract is for computer aided dispatch, which I want to be clear is an extremely important and vital tool that we have ...
It is, believe it or not, a form of surveillance."
"Two weeks ago, I flagged to the mayor's office and to various people on council that there were a bunch of things found in this contract that have nothing to do with computer aided dispatch.

There was an amendment provided, and I think that in the future, if the administration would communicate and literally respond to emails about this, there could be less tension about if that amendment satisfies concerns — because as written, it doesn't."
"I'd like to read from the community review board's description of the drone pilot program.
While the docks are placed in specific locations, the drones can be piloted remotely and are equipped with computer aided dispatch systems.
In this exhibit, there are drones that may be purchased with this.
It seems like computer aided dispatch can involve drones."
"Another form of upgrading computer aided dispatch is a tool called FUSIS."
"If this is not the intent, don't let other agencies departments use these funds."
